 The student lending landscape underwent a major transformation in 2026. New federal student loan policies, evolving borrower needs and ongoing college affordability challenges reshaped how students and families finance higher education.
 For credit unions, one lesson stood out: demand for fair-value private student loan solutions is growing.
 Federal student loan changes reshaped the market
 The biggest development of 2026 was the implementation of the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB), which brought major changes to federal student lending, including:
 Elimination of Grad PLUS loans for new borrowers (removing a major funding source for graduate and professional students)
 Caps on Parent PLUS borrowing
 Changes to federal graduate student loan limits
 Restructured repayment plans, including the elimination of SAVE
 As a result, many students and families found themselves seeking additional ways to fund educational expenses, particularly for graduate and professional degree programs.
 Graduate lending emerged as a major growth opportunity
 The most significant trend of 2026 was the surge in private lending to graduate students.
 In August and September 2026, combined graduate loan disbursement volume across the Student Choice credit union network increased more than 250% year-over-year. The increase reflected growing demand from graduate and professional students seeking alternatives to federal funding in light of OBBB changes.
 Graduate school lending is no longer a niche opportunity in the student loan world. It has become an essential part of a comprehensive education lending strategy.
 Undergraduate financing remains important
 While graduate lending drew much of the attention, undergraduate students and families continued to face funding challenges as college costs outpaced available aid. Add in the new caps on Parent PLUS and it’s clear that credit unions have a growing opportunity to help families bridge funding gaps with affordable, responsible financing solutions.
 Education lines of credit, flexible repayment options and financial guidance can help members make informed borrowing decisions while strengthening long-term relationships.
 Refinance demand continued to grow
 Shifting federal repayment programs and interest rate considerations led many borrowers to reevaluate their education debt strategies in 2026. Student loan refinancing remains an opportunity for credit unions to help members simplify repayment, secure more favorable loan terms and stay on track financially after graduation.
 Looking ahead to a new chapter
 As the student lending market continues to evolve, credit unions should focus on:
 Meeting the growing needs of graduate and professional students
 Providing flexible financing options for undergraduate students and families
 Maintaining competitive refinance programs
 Educating members on changing borrowing and repayment options
 Building productive member relationships that extend far beyond graduation
 Credit unions that view student lending as a long-term growth and relationship strategy—not just a seasonal lending opportunity—will be best positioned to succeed in the years ahead.
 CU Student Choice is evolving alongside the market with specialized lending solutions for undergraduate, graduate, professional and refinance borrowers. As member needs continue to change, credit unions have an opportunity to play an even greater role in helping students and families achieve their educational goals.
 Connect with us to start planning for a successful 2027—and beyond.
